Existential gate Exogenous uncertainty 04 / 15

Geopolitical & Trade Volatility

Sudden, systemic disruption of a specific trade corridor.

What it looks like Illustrative scenario

A Saskatchewan farmer and a Cebu brewmaster agree on one container of premium malting barley. Between signing and sailing, a tariff notice and a port slowdown land on the corridor between them. Neither price nor fit has changed. Both now prefer to wait, and waiting kills the deal.

Scenario: One Container of Barley

How an AI intervention works AI Risk Insulation

The damage is not the shock itself but the option value of delay: when a corridor might close, holding cash beats committing it. Risk insulation makes the commitment survivable. The contract is written against live feeds from customs registries and freight indices, and carries formulas agreed in advance: who absorbs a tariff step, when cargo is re-routed, what triggers a clean exit. Semantic matching adds a quieter effect, steering new pairings away from corridors that are already volatile.

How traditional markets cope

  • Futures and price hedgesuntil the risk is the route, not the price
  • Trading houses with many routesuntil they blend your specialty into commodity
  • Letter of credituntil the documents cannot be presented because the cargo never moved
